function.name: bash
function.arguments:
{"command":"cd /tmp/connected-e2e.o45aUqRf/home/canvases/cv_leztya3v7wrx/work

MAIN='Our benchmark'
FEAT=f_zfkqig6dlqas

CH2=f_fnukjapqwowq

DOC=$(canvas frame add $CV --kind doc --name "Vector database brief" --json '{"part":"Vector database brief"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "DOC=$DOC"

COVER=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":":::cover {status=\"Draft\"}\n# Vector database brief\n\nFive stores shortlisted for the search re-platform: about 40M embeddings at 768 dimensions, filtered by tenant, with hybrid keyword search.\n\nEvidence: our own benchmark, 2 Nov 2026.\n:::"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "COVER=$COVER"

S1=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"# What we compared"}' | jq -er .id)
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"The shortlist is five stores. Three are open source — Qdrant and Milvus under Apache 2.0, Weaviate under BSD-3 — one is a Postgres extension under the PostgreSQL licence, and one, Pinecone, is proprietary and managed only.[^1] They differ most in how much we run ourselves and what we pay for it."}'
echo "S1=$S1"

S2=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"# How they compare"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "S2=$S2"
LEAD=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"Our benchmark is the only side-by-side evidence we have: 10M sample vectors at 768 dimensions, tenant filter on, one four-node budget. On it Qdrant is fastest at {='\''Our benchmark'\''!B5} ms p95 latency, Milvus recalls most at {='\''Our benchmark'\''!C6}, and Pinecone — fully managed, no index build — costs the most at {='\''Cost by store'\''!B3} a month. pgvector is the cheapest at {='\''Cost by store'\''!B2} and the easiest to run, but is last on both latency ({='\''Our benchmark'\''!B2} ms) and recall ({='\''Our benchmark'\''!C2})."}' | jq -er .id)
echo "LEAD=$LEAD"

T1=$(canvas embed $CV --into $DOC --of "$MAIN!A1:F6" | jq -er .id)
canvas patch $CV $T1 --json '{"caption":"Our benchmark, 2 Nov 2026 — 10M vectors, 768-d, tenant filter on, one four-node budget","figureSource":"Our benchmark!A1:F6"}'
echo "T1=$T1"

E1=$(canvas embed $CV --into $DOC --of $CH1 | jq -er .id)
canvas patch $CV $E1 --json '{"caption":"p95 latency by store (ms, lower is better)","figureSource":"Our benchmark!A1:B6"}'
E2=$(canvas embed $CV --into $DOC --of $CH2 | jq -er .id)
canvas patch $CV $E2 --json '{"caption":"Monthly cost by store (lower is better)","figureSource":"Cost by store!A1:B6"}'
echo "E1=$E1 E2=$E2"

canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"Latency and recall move together and mostly rule nothing out: four of the five sit within 8 ms of each other and within two points of recall, so none is disqualified on quality. Cost separates them more sharply — Pinecone is roughly twice pgvector — and operating effort separates them most: Pinecone needs nothing from us, Milvus carries the most moving parts."}'

S3=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"# Feature fit"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "S3=$S3"
T2=$(canvas embed $CV --into $DOC --of "Feature fit!A1:D6" | jq -er .id)
canvas patch $CV $T2 --json '{"caption":"Feature fit, recorded from our notes","figureSource":"Feature fit!A1:D6"}'
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"Licensing and deployment are settled: Qdrant and Milvus are Apache 2.0, Weaviate BSD-3, pgvector keeps the PostgreSQL licence, and Pinecone is proprietary. Hybrid search is the gap. Our notes record it as built in for Weaviate alone (BM25 plus vectors); for the other four they say nothing, so hybrid support is unverified and must be proven in a pilot rather than assumed.[^3]"}'

S4=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"# Recommendation"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "S4=$S4"
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"Choose Qdrant. It is the only store that leads a measure that matters — the best p95 latency at {='\''Our benchmark'\''!B5} ms — while sitting at the second-lowest monthly cost ({='\''Cost by store'\''!B5}) and at the top of the recall band ({='\''Our benchmark'\''!C5}). Its payload filtering maps cleanly onto the per-tenant filter, and its Apache-2.0 core keeps the exit open. What would change this: if operating effort is the binding constraint, pgvector wins on the lowest ops score ({='\''Our benchmark'\''!F2}) and the lowest cost while staying inside our existing RDS; if we would rather run nothing at all, Pinecone is the lowest-ops option ({='\''Our benchmark'\''!F3}) at the highest price. If the pilot shows Weaviate is the only one whose hybrid search passes our acceptance tests, reconsider it at {='\''Cost by store'\''!B4} a month."}')

canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":":::callout {kind=\"risk\"}\nThe evidence is one internal benchmark (10M vectors, 768-d, tenant filter on, one budget) rather than the 40M production shape, and no independent source was reachable to check it this week — the vendor pages could not be read. Hybrid-search support is stated for Weaviate alone and unverified for the rest. Treat this as a shortlist for a paid pilot, not a final decision: run the same acceptance queries, at 40M documents and with the tenant filter on, before committing.\n:::"}'

S5=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"# References"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "S5=$S5"
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"[^1]: [Vector DB notes](canvas-cite:f_7wtm4ou3zj5b#) — our notes on the five candidates and their licences."}'
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"[^2]: [Our benchmark](canvas-cite:f_7q2zpbbbpq2x#A1:F6) — our test, 2 Nov 2026."}'
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":"[^3]: [Feature fit](canvas-cite:f_zfkqig6dlqas#A1:D6) — features recorded from our notes."}'
canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --json '{"text":":::references\n:::"}'

KF=$(canvas put $CV --parent $DOC --type text --after $COVER --json '{"text":":::key-findings {sections=\"'\''$S1,$S2,$S3,$S4'\''\"}\n1. Qdrant is fastest on our benchmark, at {='\''Our benchmark'\''!B5} ms p95 latency, with {='\''Our benchmark'\''!C5} recall.\n2. Cost runs from {='\''Cost by store'\''!B2} (pgvector) to {='\''Cost by store'\''!B3} (Pinecone) a month — a roughly two-times spread.\n3. Operating effort is the widest gap: Pinecone scores {='\''Our benchmark'\''!F3}, Milvus {='\''Our benchmark'\''!F6}, on a 1-to-5 scale.\n4. Hybrid search is unverified for four of the five; only Weaviate states it in our notes.\n:::"}' | jq -er .id)
echo "KF=$KF"
echo "DONE DOC=$DOC""}
